sources.entry: Should I Become a Manager? - Cap Watkins

summary.title: Should I Become a Manager?
summary.one_liner: Four lessons from Cap Watkins on choosing between a management track and staying a senior individual contributor: management is a fresh start, contributor growth is slower, accountability matters, and the move is reversible.
keywords: moving back from management to ic
takeaways: Becoming a manager is essentially starting over: new skills like navigating the organization, building processes, and managing 1:1s.
Contributor tracks often offer slower advancement and less pay and authority than management tracks, especially at growing companies.
Consider whether you want to be accountable for team outcomes; each management level can differ greatly from the one before.
Nobody feels fully ready; caring about doing well is a good sign, and direct experience is the best teacher.
Management is reversible: people can and do move back to design, engineering, or product roles.
summary.summary: The author, who has spoken with many people facing this career choice, shares four pieces of advice drawn from personal experience and conversations. He argues that becoming a manager is like starting over, that contributor tracks usually advance more slowly than management tracks, and that the decision hinges on whether you want the accountability that comes with the role. He also says no one is ever fully ready, and that the move is reversible, using a story about his first 1:1 with his own manager. The piece is an opinion essay rather than a how-to guide.
